text_fidelity_a:
LEGO Star Wars: A New Hope Imperial Star Destroyer 75252 Building Kit (4,784 Pieces) The first thing I noticed about this set was the weight. This is the first LEGO set that I've gotten that I would actually describe as heavy. That's a lot of brick. The box is nice, and contains several smaller boxes. Those boxes have some blueprint art on them, but no useful labeling as to where to begin. You need to open them all anyway, because the unlabeled bags of large parts are mixed in with some of the later bags, despite being needed early on. The bag numbering only goes up to about 20, but there are many bags for each number and the bags have bags in them. The instruction book is huge and spiral bound, with some nice history in the early pages.

The set goes together surprisingly quickly early on, starting with the display base and docking clamps, which the ship is built on, with sections being build and then clipped on. The internal support structure is well engineered and solid. You get a good impression of the overall size and shape of the ship by the time you are done with bag 2.

At first glance, this may look like a tedious grey set where all the parts look the same, but the insides are brightly colored. This is really nice because the parts being built are often rotated between panels, and the colors really help with both finding the parts and orienting with the instructions. When you're done, it also makes it easy to spot anything you missed, because the grey exterior will have rainbow colors there.

One disappointment is the thin area down the sides of the ship. I like them fine individually, but the instructions have you build them identically, so rather than being bilaterally symmetrical, one side looks like it's upside down compared to the other. I understand this saved them some pages, and made construction a little easier, but I would've appreciated a heads up so I could build it mirrored, since I think that would've worked out fine, at least for the greebles on the outside. I may actually take one side apart and redo it, though It's the kind of detail that an observer might not notice because this thing is so big. There are other areas that are more obviously asymmetrical, which is true to the movie, but looks really jarring to me the way they implemented it.

After completing it, I feel like it was designed by two different teams of people. The interior structure is an awesome feat of engineering, and so sturdy you can carry the whole thing by an interior handle, despite its great weight, and they did it with all existing parts. The exterior is about as expected in a Lego set. The transition between the two is weak. Brushing against it risks knocking things off. Sometimes it's just some barely attached pieces on the back, other times something obviously comes apart inside that's going to take some doing to get to and fix. The different sections are often just resting loosely on each other and sometimes look uneven. There is a tiny and comically inadequate clip to hold the four sections of the front in alignment. You may want to think about what you're going to do with it when it's done. It's large, heavy, and oddly shaped. Comes on a nice stand though.

text_fidelity_a:
Green Toys Farm Playset - 13 Piece Pretend Play, Motor Skills, Language & Communication Kids Role Play Toy. No BPA, phthalates, PVC. Dishwasher Safe, Recycled Plastic, Made in USA, Red, Pack of 1 I really like that green toys uses recycled plastic and makes a variety of very simple, imagination based toys that are fun for kids to play with. This toy really seems to have a lot of potential in that regard. There are large barn doors on both sides of the barn that open and shut, and it open and airy second level where the sheep and pigs can hang out and look out the window, etc.

The fencing and the little covered area presumably for a trough are getting ignored at our house, I have a three-year-old and a not quite one-year-old, but the barn itself, simple animals, and truck were greeted with boos and eyes upon opening, and have been in play ever since, not only with the things that came in the set but with their other toys, which is really what one hopes when buying an open-ended toy like this. The truck has enough room to put action figures, Lego bricks, pig, etc. in there, and the barn is the same.

I have one quibble, actually two: while the barn seems like it should fit the truck, when you try to close the doors, the truck squirts out the back doors. When you go to close the back doors, it squirts out the front doors. There's not enough room in the barn to park the truck, even though (and this is what my problem with it is) it looks like it was meant to be parked in there. My toddler can be a little bit uptight about these types of things and when he is in a bad mood, this failure of the truck to park properly in the barn really upsets him. How hard would it have been to design these figures so that they all worked gracefully together? I think many toddlers would have really appreciated that thoughtful touch.

My other minor quibble is that the cow figures stand on two legs and are dressed as farmers. We try to present things that are at least a little bit based in reality to our children of this age, and so a cow dressed as a farmer would not have been my first choice. I would've preferred one farmer and one cow that actually looked like a cow, or two cows and no farmer, if they were worried about what color of plastic to make a farmer so that it appealed to everybody. I think they wanted a farmer figure to sit in the truck and drive it, and that is nice but not 100% necessary.

Overall, this is an awesome set and would make a fabulous gift for families that have kids of different ages. I personally am getting rid of the fencing and covered outdoor red thing, plus the weird cow farmers, but the base set – a barn, some pigs and sheep, and the truck, are awesome. Even though you would give the gift perhaps to one child, it is nice that everybody can play with it, it is not gender-based, and it has potential to be played with in a variety of ways as the child or children grow. Another win for green toys!
text_fidelity_b: Green Toys Farm Playset - 13 Piece Pretend Play, Motor Skills, Language & Communication Kids Role Play Toy. No BPA, phthalates, PVC. Dishwasher Safe, Recycled Plastic, Made in USA, Red, Pack of 1

Glitter Girls - Convertible Car for 14-inch Dolls - Toys, Clothes & Accessories for Girls 3-Year-Old & Up, Blue, Orange, Pink This convertible car for 14 inch dolls is completely awesome. We have a number of glitter girls dolls and two of them can fit into this convertible with ease, along with one of the glitter girls puppies sitting on a lap.

My kids saw this in a Christmas catalog and were completely enchanted with it, asking for it over and over again. It's about as big as you would expect given that the glitter girls both have to fit in there, and it has a dashboard that opens, a little side container that opens in between the two seats, two cupholders, and the trunk.

We have the glitter girls sweetshop and the accessories sweetshop that has some delightful cups of confectionery beverage, and I was delighted to find that these sweetshop beverages fit into the cupholders perfectly. (They also fit into the girls hands). The dashboard has very little room to put things in when it's open, and the angle is such that things really don't stay put very well at the dashboard is open, so I would've liked a little bit better design on that, because my kids had to work hard to find something they wanted to bring along that was small enough to fit. Same thing with the little container in between the two seats, if that could have been just a little bit wider, it would get used even more.

The trunk is also a little small and again the shape of the interior of it makes it harder for things to fit in, because it is just a rectangular box opening that is kind of slick, so when you put things in the kind of want to slide out. There is enough room in the car to where they could have made the trunk much more substantial, and it would've made this an even cooler car.

That said, these are just quibbles and the real proof of whether a toy is any good is in the pudding. My kids love it, and they've been playing with it nonstop and vrooming the girls around on all kinds of adventures since the car arrived. I've been delighted to see the amount of imaginative play that has taken place with the addition of a car, to where the girls can leave the bedroom and go on all kinds of fun adventures.

The car seems well-made and is very sturdy, the doors open, and if you need to put the windshield down for storage, it does fold down. Overall this is a great toy if you have 14 inch dolls who need some adventure in their lives.
text_fidelity_b: Glitter Girls - Convertible Car for 14-inch Dolls - Toys, Clothes & Accessories for Girls 3-Year-Old & Up, Blue, Orange, Pink

text_fidelity_a:
KidKraft Deluxe Let's Cook Kitchen, Gift for Ages 3+ I bought this for my 2 year old son for Christmas, I mean Santa dropped this off for my son for Christmas because he loves to come into my kitchen and pull out all the pots and pans and grab every utensil in the drawers to, "mix, mix, mix" as he says. So, why not a kitchen. The world's greatest chefs are men so why can't my son get a head start. My concern is that he is so tall I needed a kitchen that he could grow into. I also wanted something basic that he would pretend to cook instead of pushing pushing buttons on gadgets that whirred, chirp, and buzz. So, a wooden kitchen was the way to go, not plastic. I settled on this one because it's not pink and the dimensions seemed to be appropriate.

Pros:
If you have a tall two year old, this is the kitchen for you. My son is in the 95% for height. I am 5'10" and everyone else in my family is tall, so you have an idea of how tall he is. It will be at least a year before the counter is at a counter height that adults would expect a counter to be. Currently, it stands at his bottom of his breast bone. He's currently about 36* tall.

Once you put it together, it's sturdy and it comes lots of extra screws and parts just in case, which I needed.

The pot holder and the spatula and spoon you see in the picture also come with it.

The instructions were no more difficult that an Ikea set of a directions.

The hours of playtime during the Christmas break and the look on his face and level of excitement was priceless.

Cons:

You will need two sized Phillips head screwdrivers, a wrench or a set of pliers, and at least FOUR hours to put this together. So, slow down on the egg nog.

It's made of particle board and the overlay is paper not painted so it chips off easily.

It's HEAVY! Over 70 pounds!

OFF GASSING! This is the biggest downfall, which I should have known, but just didn't think of. This product offgasses something terrible! Because the box is extremely heavy and because it was delivered to my front door I just couldn't get this down to the basement or to the garage. (I live in an older, well-established neighborhood where most of the houses are pre-1950, so if your house has a garage in the front of the house unlike mine, which is down a driveway and to the back, try to get the UPS man to take it there!) I could only open the box in the house on Christmas Eve, and thus, the offgassing of the kitchen was really terrible and made me nauseous. I would highly recommend airing it out for at least a week in your garage before you put it together and bring it into your house.

Therefore, the toxic chemicals we no doubt inhaled because of my inability to air this product out is a big reason why this only a three not a four star rating.

Overall, I'm satisfied because my son is happy and loves it. If I had the money or space, I would have just purchased the Pottery Barn kitchen set or if I had the time, I would have just made one inspired from Pinterest, but it was a good $150.00 spent, and I'm sure we'll have it for a long time.
text_fidelity_b: KidKraft Deluxe Let's Cook Kitchen, Gift for Ages 3+

PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Easy-to-Build 6-in-1 Coding Robots for Kids with Puzzles, Augmented Reality STEM Toy, Ages 4,5,6,7,8,9,10+ Year Old Boys and Girls (App Based) I like the size of the pieces because I have kids in my home who like legos and with those it can be hard to find pieces because they are so small and they end up all over the place. I also like the color combination that was provided. The instructions have to be accessed through a website, which is okay, but I would have liked to have paper directions (but that's just a personal preference).

What I like: 1) within the app it provides step by step directions to build the characters. You have to press play through each step therefore you move along at your own pace. You can also flip the image around so you can see the sides, front, and bottom of the chracter (how it should be) so you can make sure everything is in the right spot. 2) the pieces are very sturdy. I don't forsee myself having a problem with them breaking unless its intentional. 3) it charges really quickly. The block that is the main piece of the entire item is rechargeable. After playing with it for sometime the battery indicated it was on 17% (through the app) and it only took about 20 minutes to fully charge.

What I didn't like: 1) the app is a pain. The description states the item is optimized for android devices with android 7.0 or more, but this is not true. I have three tablets and a samsung chromebook with android 7.0 or more, but when I go to the appstore, it says the app is not optimized for my device or I cannot find the app at all. I had to download the app on my Galaxy S9. Which I would rather the kids be able to play with it on their own devices instead of my phone. I also added it to an iphone XR and it worked. 2) the app isn't the best functionally. It would shut off on me randomly or freeze up. It even caused my phone to go black for about five minutes and after plugging it into the charger and waiting, it finally popped up on camera mode. 3) it is not always easy or fast getting the phone and the item to connect. You have to have your location and bluetooth on and even when the device is powered on, the app will tell you to power it on. Then half the time, it takes 3-5 minutes to finally connect. 4) I like to coding part, because you can do an order of functions, but when you want to just play with it, you can only go back and forth or right and left, depending on the character you built. We built an alligator and it just opened and closed its mouth and not with the same force each time.

Overall, It's a nice toy, but I would not purchase it for $99
text_fidelity_b: PAI TECHNOLOGY Botzees Easy-to-Build 6-in-1 Coding Robots for Kids with Puzzles, Augmented Reality STEM Toy, Ages 4,5,6,7,8,9,10+ Year Old Boys and Girls (App Based)

text_fidelity_a:
Mini Human Skeleton Model for Anatomy, 17.7'' Full Body Human Skeleton Model with Movable Arms and Legs on Plastic Base for Medical Teaching Learning, Kids Learning Education Display Tool Gift Wow, is this a toy? Because it is full of problems and inaccuracies. I’d like to start with my side-by-side photo showing some of the most egregious problems.
On the right hand with a black background is how it is supposed to look, and on the left is how it actually looks.
*Spinal alignment: any human with this type of alignment has a serious medical condition. The spine is supposed to have curvature in order to support the weight properly. As you can see by the Sideview of this toy, there is minimal curvature, and what little there is would lead the person to fall backwards. This is particularly problematic along the cervical and lumbar vertebrae (neck and lower back)
*The ribcage on this silly toy flares out at the bottom in a bizzarre way that doesn’t represent normal anatomy. Likewise, there is no attempt to indicate where the bone ends and the cartilaginous attachment points begin. Our ribs are not solid bone all the way from the vertebral column to the sternum. There’s supposed to be cartilage toward the midline as the ribs approach the sternum. Even if this model can’t indicate that, there should at least have been some sort of scoring or line or something.
The radius and ulna are ridiculous. Their thickness and size are not in correct proportion with the rest of the body. Also, why is this not in anatomical position?
Then there’s the attachment from the humerus to the glenoid fossa of the scapula, which cannot be seen in the poster or in this model. That’s just not how our arms are attached at all. Like the hip joint, the shoulder is a ball and socket joint, albeit a much shallower one than the hips. The way this is attached is so misleading and terrible. I can’t even deal with it. And circling back once again to the alignment of the spine, the pelvic bowl is completely wrong. It’s supposed to tilt downward much more.
So basically this is garbage. It’s not good for art, and it’s not really good for teaching either. What a shame. It did have some things going for it, but the issues I pointed out are too significant to ignore.
The included poster is OK, and so are a few of the skull details. It gets to stars for effort and that. But it’s pretty obvious to me that whoever designed this doesn’t know their anatomy. Imagine how much better they could’ve done if they actually paid a professional to do the design before manufacturing hundreds (thousands?) of useless little skeletons.
text_fidelity_b: Mini Human Skeleton Model for Anatomy, 17.7'' Full Body Human Skeleton Model with Movable Arms and Legs on Plastic Base for Medical Teaching Learning, Kids Learning Education Display Tool Gift

Rolife DIY Book Nook Kits Time Travel, 3D Wooden Puzzles Bookshelf Insert Decorative Bookend Model Kits with LED, DIY Crafts/Birthday Gifts/Home Decor for Girls&Boys Teens&Adults (Time Travel) I've seen these decorative bookends before, but they're rather pricey. So when I saw one that wasn't as expensive and looked like it would be a fun project, I decided to give it a try. I've always enjoyed crafts and a recent project was assembling and decorating an entire dollhouse.
That project, which took a couple of months, was nowhere near as frustrating as this, which took two days (when I'm determined, I'm determined).
Note that there's only ONE bookend in the kit. The first photo pictures two, but there's only one per kit. The kit comes with glue, a screwdriver, two lights, instructions, and everything you need except the batteries to power the lights. I would HIGHLY recommend that you provide a strong glue such as super glue or a really good wood glue for this project. You'll need it if my experience is anything to go by while building it.
I also recommend that you don't pop out the pieces beforehand, but do it while building (unless you are the type to label everything after you do that). There are a LOT of pieces to keep track of, and the labels aren't printed on them. Resist the temptation.
Now, for the kit itself. The instructions are NOT the best. There's 30+ pages, and very few words. It's basically illustrations and there were times when I feel steps were skipped. I had to figure out on my own which light when where (the shorter light for the door lamp, the longer one for the top light). Things like that. It was very frustrating.
Also, the kit is made out of a composite wood and has many, MANY tiny parts. Some parts that you have to push through tiny openings and through multiple openings. As careful as I was, these pieces broke. Hence the need for a really good, strong glue. The glue was also needed to keep pieces together. There were so many times that parts fell off when they shouldn't have, so gluing them together helped to move things along.
Oh, and I'd put pieces together only to have the instructions have pieces added later, and I'd be all 'why didn't they have me add this piece earlier'? Especially when you're pushing delicate pieces together.
If you've a miniature magnetic screwdriver, use it instead. The included screws are tiny and you're trying to get them in very small holes while screwing at awkward angles. Not having to worry about them falling will really help.
There was a lot of swearing involved with this project, I will not lie. I'm not sure this is a project for a kid, 14+ or older, unless they really like kit-building. Maybe if it was built out of better material. I debated what to rate it, but since it turned out looking good in the end (with the help of a lot of extra glue), I went with three stars. The finished product is lovely and the lights work, it was just very frustrating to get there.
text_fidelity_b: Rolife DIY Book Nook Kits Time Travel, 3D Wooden Puzzles Bookshelf Insert Decorative Bookend Model Kits with LED, DIY Crafts/Birthday Gifts/Home Decor for Girls&Boys Teens&Adults (Time Travel)

Minnie Mouse's Home Sweet Headquarters is a 4-level dollhouse playset with five rooms of play and features three figures, 12 play pieces, an elevator, and Minnie's magic Turnstyler fashion closet. This little Minne Mouse playhouse is just adorable! Perfect for toddlers and preschool children. It is a replica of Minnie's house from the Disney Channel, Disney Junior show called, "Happy Helpers Adventures." The playhouse is called, "Minnie Mouse's Home Sweet Headquarters," and in the show it is located in the town of Hot Dog Hills. This house is not just Minnie's home on the show, but it is also the business headquarters for Minnie and Daisy Duck's business, "Happy Helpers." The house has five rooms and four levels. There is a cute elevator leading to the second floor, and a "Turnstyler" closet which contains three different Happy Helpers outfits (note they are pictures of clothing rather than actual clothing that a child could put on Minnie).

Minnie's Home Sweet Headquarters set includes three 3-inch poseable figures, Minnie, Daisy, and Figaro (the kitty from the film, Pinnochio), as well as 12 accessory play pieces, including two beds, a vanity, and two desks just like the ones on the Disney show. There are also a spa tub, a hairdryer, and an oven and serving cart in the kitchen, and Figaro has his own pet food and bowl.

This play house requires a small bit of assembly, but even I managed it easily, and I am definitely not good at putting things together.

I really appreciate that this is not a typical empty doll house. It's great that it comes with furniture and other interesting pieces and the three occupants, who are the main characters from a child-favorite Disney TV show, Daisy Duck, Figaro and, of course, Minnie Mouse. There are lots of lovely, bright colors throughout the house, with Minnie's signature color of pink predominating. I especially am impressed with the little elevator that goes up and down, the rotating closet and the fact that the house's doors open and close.

This has turned out to be a very popular gift with my 20-month-old granddaughter. She loves it now, and she can continue to enjoy for several more years to come.

A terrific Christmas present!
text_fidelity_b: Minnie Mouse's Home Sweet Headquarters is a 4-level dollhouse playset with five rooms of play and features three figures, 12 play pieces, an elevator, and Minnie's magic Turnstyler fashion closet.

Thames & Kosmos TK1 Telescope Plus Astronomy Educational Science Kit | Refractor 60/700 | Aluminum Full Size Tripod with Altazimuth Mount | 35X, 70X, 140X Power | Parents' Choice Recommended The telescope itself is really very good. Even with the lowest magnification lens attached The Housemate and I were able to see Saturn and discern the gap between the planet and its rings. With a higher magnification, things became much clearer, and even more exciting. The first clear image of the moon took my breath away.

The drawbacks? It's very hard to use standing up. I realize it's made for children, but I think a taller tripod might have been a plus here. Even sitting we had to hunch down to see anything at a 45 degree angle or above. Also, the viewfinder did not help at all. I found all the objects we wanted to see by sighting along the barrel of the telescope itself. Now possibly I attached the viewfinder the wrong way, though there really only seems to be one way to do it. Either way, we saw what we intended to see which made the exercise worthwhile.

Why a telescope? Aren't you and your children worth it? Don't you want to learn more about even our part of the universe? This is an amazing gift for the children in your life, or even for yourself. It's lightweight and easy to transport and with the help of something like Google Sky, you can figure out what it is you're looking at with ease. It's a step on the road to becoming better educated in Astronomy, and it should spark a sense of wonder anyone who looks up and longs to know more.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos TK1 Telescope Plus Astronomy Educational Science Kit | Refractor 60/700 | Aluminum Full Size Tripod with Altazimuth Mount | 35X, 70X, 140X Power | Parents' Choice Recommended

LeapFrog LeapStart Interactive Learning System, Pink Mix feelings about this product. Had it over a year with minimal travel usage. We usually leave it in our dining room on our kids table so they can do activities while mom cooks. We loved it when it worked but once the batteries died and I replaced the device with new batteries, it turns on and does nothing. It doesn't sense the stylus. It will on a random occasion after multiple attempts say one or two words when pointed on the stylus but then stops again. Changed batteries out a couple of times and unfortunately didn't help. Now, I have two disappointed kids with numerous of these books and told family to get more books for Christmas which will only be to their disappointment that they have no device to use them with.

As for when the device worked, we would loved it and would recommend to any parent with kids under 7. My son is almost 5yo son and 3yo daughter love this. They take turns using it since I only had one of the Leap Start devices but numerous books. My daughter was heart broken after multiple attempts to try new batteries.

I hate to give one start but given the longevity of this product for the price, it needs to last more than a year. I mean one year for a $45 device. Maybe some would say that's worth it but not when you shell out $10 - $15 on each of the books. I might of gotten a faulty device so maybe it's just poor luck on my part.

UPDATE—7/1118
We’ve had our new leapstart book (this time I bought at big box store with a warranty) for 5 months now since the last broke, so far so good but I’m still not sure on longevity still, however i have changed batteries a few times since we use ours alot and have had no issues. I am adding a star as my kids fight over this all the time. I’ve got 6yo boy who LOVES it who is also my reader and 4yo girl who always wants what her brother has but genuinely love this thing. I struggle with getting my kids to play with their $100 toy they got for Christmas but love this thing and it’s a plus for me since it’s educational. So i still can’t give this item as high of a star as I would like because of durability I would recommend it if you don’t care if you have to replace it. I’m glad I did but recommend getting some warranty because after investing in the books and how much my kids like It, you may want to get another.
text_fidelity_b: LeapFrog LeapStart Interactive Learning System, Pink

ATTELANTY Diabolo——Chinese yoyo (Blue, 3.9 inch*5.1 inch) Having a teen who likes to expel excess energy by goofing around with his standard style yo-yo.. I knew when he saw this online.. it would make a great stocking stuffer and challenge. I LOVE to promote any activity that gives one a break from screen time..!! This teaches much more then a trick using talent- it promotes focus, patience and dare I say practiced discipline!? A win/win for me..

Ordered in the larger size I was mistaken by actual measurements given- and for any who may not know.. take note: the sizes printed are just for the cups itself.. So, this was surprisingly bigger than anything I had anticipated!! Length is 18” in the sticks alone.. along with length of the yo-yo itself. ** see photos included for actual size idea..

Cup portion is made of a hollowed plastic and does appear durable- however, the sticks may be a different story! Thinner and in the longer length- makes these more vulnerable to breaking.. i’m certain there’s a purpose for the lightweight material being used in construction- my guess it’s necessary to perform the actual tricks?! One should just be careful to have plenty of clearance from hard objects when learning/practicing.. hitting into a solid item could potentially cause these to break! Definitely an item for older kids/adults.. Otherwise these may be a bit too fragile!! Priced at $35- it does seem a bit excessive for the actual materials used.. however, if enjoyed- it may end up $ well spent.

Retro Handheld Game Console, Portable Video Game Console with 400 Classical 8 Bit FC Games 2.8 Inch Screen 1020MAh Rechargeable Battery Support Connecting TV (Blue) I love the old console games and I looked to this handheld to revisit some of the older games I remember enjoying several years ago. For the price this is a decent little console and I like it, though there is some room for improvement.

In the past, playing the older games required downloading a ROM and putting it into an emulator, and if you knew where to look for ROMs you could find hundreds of them, many familiar and even more that were very unfamiliar. I expected this little console to be something silimar to the old emulator, preloaded with old ROMs, and it seems to be fairly close to that. There are many games I recognize that are a lot fo fun to revisit, and there are a lot of games that are unfamiliar.

This console comes preloaded with several hundred games of varying types and quality. As mentioned there are quite a few that are familiar, but many that I never saw in an arcade. Some appear to be Asian releases that never were released here.

Navigation is a minor pain. If you want to play a game that is far down the list, you have to navigate there every time. There doesn't appear to be any memory for last games played.

Another minor disappointment is that several titles are listed more than once in the menu. This suggests to me that there are different versions, even if I can't tell what the differences are.

I'm thinking this is the same thing as the old emulators that can be found online and it just packaged in a handheld and preloaded with ROMs. That's fine by me, I like those old games. It would have been nice to provide better navigation, though, and maybe reduce the versions of each game to the latest or most bug-free? For the cost, it's a worthwhile system if you love those old games.
text_fidelity_b: Retro Handheld Game Console, Portable Video Game Console with 400 Classical 8 Bit FC Games 2.8 Inch Screen 1020MAh Rechargeable Battery Support Connecting TV (Blue)

This opens up possibilities like training exercises and real-time online competitions. The app is actually pretty excellent here, unlike another cube we tried, this one actually has competitors and it seems to work (however my son is suspicious that they might not be real players. We tried the app on a few different devices in our home, with processors from Qualcomm Snapdragon and other's with Samsung's Exynos (flagship Galaxy S level hardware). It doesn't seem to be the phone/tablet that is the problem, but rather that the cube isn't always registering the movement to send to the app. This causes things to get out of alignment relatively quickly, especially when speed solving, and renders the entire experience frustrating.
This had so much potential, we're really disappointed.

Mattel Games Apples to Apples 15th Appleversary Edition My boyfriend and I never heard of this game and this is their 15th "Appleversary" Edition.

This game is for ages 12+ with 4-8 players. Included in the box are:
- One game instruction sheet
- 441 Black Apple Cards
- 63 White Apple Cards
- 25 Scoring Tokens

After all the like colored cards are combined and shuffled (good luck shuffling 441 cards; I couldn't do it), the cards get stored face-down in the plastic game tray/box they came in along with the tokens.

The game of play is as follows:
- Each of the 4 or more players are dealt 5 black cards each.
- The one player in each round who is the judge picks one white card and chooses one of the two words on the cards. He or she then says the word out loud and places the card face up on the table.
- The remaining players pick a black card from their hand that they think best describes the word being played. They put that card face own in the center and when all the players have submitted their card, the black cards in the center get mixed up.
- The judge then reads each card aloud and the player who submitted that card makes their case to the judge of why their card best exemplifies the word being played.
- The player who won their case with the judge gets a token.
- The play then continues to the left with the card decks and judging responsibility becoming the role of the next player. Each player whose card count is less than 5 black cards is dealt another card.
- The game ends when there is a winner with four tokens.

What makes this game so much fun is the conversation that occurs when convincing the judge. For instance, the judge might pick the word squishy and a player might pick the card about fish and say something like when you're preparing the fish and stretching it out for cooking it becomes all squishy.

My boyfriend and I loved it and found it hilarious. We even found it more challenging because the two other people we planned to play with weren't available. As a result, we wound up playing two hands a piece with one of us playing one hand when we were the judge. That brought another whole level of ridiculousness to the table. It was difficult not to pick our own selections as winners.

This game is only limited by each player's imagination and ability to argue their case. It's perfect for parties or large gatherings with 4 to 8 players.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Games Apples to Apples 15th Appleversary Edition

VTech Kidizoom Camera - 2010 Version Kids like to do grown- up things and the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera allows them to do just that. This is a fully- functioning camera specifically designed for the needs and desires of youngsters and it allows kids to take pictures, edit them in fun ways, and even upload them to a computer for further viewing and editing.

Many qualities make this camera one to consider and the first is the memory. This is sold as a child's camera, but it has a surprisingly high level of memory and is capable of holding up to 400 pictures! This is much better than I expected and with this much memory, it will take a long time before kids exceed the available space. They can walk around the house ansd snap picture after picture without worrying that the memory will fill.

Another positive aspect with the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera is its durability. This camera is made from plastic with a rubberized edge that makes it easy to hold and highly resistant to breakage. My girls have dropped it several times and it continues to work regardless. It is also very entertaining. Not only can kids take their own pictures of mom, dad, the family dog, and their friends, but they can also add to the fun by using the editing feature. The silly editing allows kids a chance to take an ordinary picture and make it look funny.

So, the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera is fun for kids, but are there any cons? Well, there are a few but they are minor enough to overlook. One is the viewing screen on the back of the camera. It is quite small and some images will be barely perceptible. It would be completely unacceptable to adults, but kids will likely find it perfectly fine. Then, one has to consider the picture quality. This camera has only 0.3 megapixels and that means the clarity of the pictures is well below average. Once again, kids are not likely to care. They will so enjoy having their own camera and taking their own pictures that they won't even notice or mind the fuzzy images.

Kids like to mimic adults and the Vtech Kidizoom Digital Camera is likely to be a hit with most youngsters for this and other reasons. As I said, the clarity of the photos isn't the best and the camera does have a few other minor flaws, but none of this will matter to most children. The ability to take their own pictures, edit them in fun ways, and even view them on a computer will be more than enough to please the young camerabug in your home.

ENJBRICK Harry Castle Potter Toy Building Set,Compatible with Lego Idea Building Blocks Kit for Kids and Adults 521pcs This set consists of thirteen #1 bags for Weasley's Wizarding Wheezes (the purple and orange building), eight #2 bags for Flourish and Blotts (the green and brown building), one bag of plates, instructions, and a small sticker sheet.

The bags are not numbered individually. Trust me, open all the bags for a building. So all #1 bags or all #2 bags. You’ll need a lot of space for the pieces, but it’s less frustrating in the long run. Steps require pieces from every bag as you go. Finding the pieces for each step took the longest part of this build.

The instructions are mostly clear*, but the build experience itself is frustrating. Some pieces stay together and some do not. I spent so much time rebuilding because a section would break when I put new pieces on. For example, the window section for WWW, I had to test window pieces to see which would stay together and then stay on the building. For the upper window section, where the arms come out, I had to redo that three or four times, carefully holding the windows together.

*Step 64 has the wrong pieces, there is a sheet to show the proper pieces.

The buildings are delicate. On my Flourish and Blotts building, the bottom barely stays together, so I can’t take it off the base. The buildings are hollow inside, so you can hide items. The F&B building has a tray inside, and the WWW building has a rod to use to pop the tray out. If I popped the tray out, I’d have to put the F&B building back together. I don’t care for the hiding space, I’d prefer buildings that were more stable, especially if they’re supposed to be bookends.

Some of the stickers go over multiple pieces, one sticker on 2 or 3 pieces. The Dark Mark sticker is misspelled: DRRK MRRK.

Overall, the finished set looks good, but getting to that finished set was a somewhat frustrating experience.
text_fidelity_b: ENJBRICK Harry Castle Potter Toy Building Set,Compatible with Lego Idea Building Blocks Kit for Kids and Adults 521pcs

Up and down seemed to be working fine, but with the drone constantly flying sideways, it was impossible to control properly. Even when using the right control stick, it seemed to only acknowledge forwards, and wouldn’t respond to the other direction. Then the drone suddenly dropped the WiFi connection within 10 minutes. Powering off and on didn’t fix it. I took the battery out, put it back in and was connected again for a minute or two before the battery just died completely. Yes, I fully charged the battery before use. Surely this products battery should last more than 15 minutes of intermittent usage.
Overall, as someone familiar with remote control devices and technology, I found this drone difficult to control and hence no fun to use.

Hot Wheels Workshop Track Builder Spin Turn Track Extension I grabbed one of these the same time as I purchased the Turn Kicker. Initially I thought this would somehow be similar, in that it would shoot the cars out of a curve, but this is different. Basically, your car goes up a small ramp, into an enclosed compartment which rotates 90 degrees and releases the car down a ramp on the opposite side of the track. The ramps's are not steep, so if you set up the Spin Turn at ground level, it won't travel too far when it gets released. What's cool is, you can either have it trigger another stunt, or set up the Spin Launch high off the ground (via books or trestles), so when a car gets dropped off on the opposite track, it will have lots of gravity to continue on.

The Usual Issue:
Upon assembly (which is super simple), once you attach the white roof to the Spin Turn's car base, you can't take it apart. It's already near impossible to put all pieces back in their box, but this just makes it a definite nope! Sounds like a recurring problem with many other Hot Wheel Sets... because it is.

I wonder if a better name could have been chosen than "Spin Launch"? It gives the impression that the car is getting launched like it does with many rubber band-triggered accessories. The car is only getting transported to another ramp. They should have called this the Turn Kicker, and the other accessory the Spin Launch.

Overall, I DO like the effect. Many stunts go so fast that it's over before you know it. This gives you a moment to at least watch it make the transfer. By all means, the transfer is quick, but not one of those blink of the eye or miss it stunts. A worthy add-on.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Workshop Track Builder Spin Turn Track Extension

text_fidelity_a: WEQIN Water Guns for Kids Adults 1200CC Squirt Guns High 3 Nozzles Capacity Water Blaster Water Toys Summer Gun Toys Water Shooter Fighting Games Play Toys… This is a great way to cool off in the heat with the kids! My little ones loved how easy it was to replenish after using up the tank (the entire back opens up so it fills much faster), and the triple-nozzle front was a blast (literally! ha). One thing I didn't realize beforehand, however, is that it works entirely by pump action. That is, unlike a super soaker or other water pistol that builds pressure with the pump and then releases with a trigger, the pump is the entire firing mechanism, and the "trigger" is just for show (doesn't do anything). Pulling back on the pump fires the water, and the strength is adjusted  by how hard/fast you pull back. My older kids were able to figure that out, but my youngest (3 years old) found it disappointing. He likes the trigger kind because it is easy for him to fire, and with this he wasn't able to figure out the dexterity to make it shoot very far. For what it is, it works and is fun, but I do sort of wish it had a trigger that wasn't just there for looks.

text_fidelity_a: Foxnovo Universal Tall Landing Gear Skid for DJI F450 F550 Sk480 Multirotor Quadcopter These legs are the perfect upgrade for the Syma X8C (white) if you're going to be using a different camera. The stock legs are just too short to allow you to mount any kind of adjustable camera rigging and GoPro type camera. You will need to do some drilling in these legs (and shave off the mounting alignment flange of the quad) to make them fit. But, it's worth it. This pic is of the same legs (black) on my Syma X8G (same body as the C, just a different color) and these legs on my Syma X8C. These legs give you the spread and stability you need, as well as the height. They're rigid, strong and don't weigh much more than the stock legs. I've seen some negative reviews regarding 'flimsiness'. I think that anyone should keep in mind the original configuration calls for bracing between the legs, in such a way that actually provides more structural integrity to each leg. Therefore, no bracing means less rigidity, the greater the chances of breakage. Having said that, I've been flying my Syma X8 quads with these for a while now. One of which was totaled. Seriously, the quad dropped like a rock from about 150 feet, crashing through trees and broke HARD. I had to do a total rebuild with new body, motor mounts, gears, etc.The only parts re-used were the control board and motors and the LEGS, which DID NOT BREAK!

All of the planes are shaped differently and they each do different tricks. We haven't figured out all the best angles yet, but my son loves watching them go and then he runs after them. The set is packed with cute details, bright colors, and play features. It might be the best Friends set I’ve ever built.

The disco arcade has 3 areas: the roller disco, the bowling lane (6 pins), and the arcade. The different areas are connected with hinges, so the set opens and closes. When it’s closed, the translucent green windows let you see inside the arcade. When it’s open, you can utilize all the different play areas without being cramped.

I really like how the building is designed to open and close! It looks cool either way. And if I compare this to a set that has an open back to access the play features, the roller rink just looks more complete.

I don’t love all the stickers, but for once I’m not going to ding the set. It would be impossible to print so many tiles. I do recommend adults help with sticker application, but the rest of the set is easily doable by a kid (6+). The instructions are clear as always with Lego. Pieces are separated into numbered bags to help with assembly (less time searching for the needed piece for a step) and to cut down slightly on mess while building.

Overall, I was really impressed by this set. It’s fun to build, fun to play with, and fun to have on display.

However it feels like some things weren't fully thought through and could have been easily made better.
For example, the spinner needle feels like it stops exactly on the line more than half the time, causing much arguing and debate over which side it actually landed. If you have ever played the game Life or used a spinning prize wheel, you know there is a much better way to do this: Have plastic borders that catch on the needle so it stops in one space clearly (and makes a cool motor noise as it click-click-clicks quickly). Once you're making giant playing pieces and a large floor mat board, this would not have added a lot of cost and would have made the game infinitely more fun and smooth to play.
And speaking of giant playing pieces, once you assemble them, they don't fit back in the box unless you break them apart, something that probably won't last if you do it every time you put the game away. It could have come with a bag or something to store the game board and pieces in. As of now, I'm pretty sure the pieces and board are going to get separated from each other in our family room. It's a fun game, but unlike giant versions of Jenga, Connect Four or Chess, the novelty of giant Sorry wears off quickly and at some point my mother-in-law actually asked why we can't just play it on the table like a regular game. It's fun for the novelty, but the caveats and game mechanics make this not worth more than 3 stars in my opinion.
text_fidelity_b: Giant Clue Classic Mystery Party Retro Board Game Summer Toy with Large Rooms, Giant Cards, and Foam Tools, for Kids and Families Ages 8 and up

Swimways Dry Float Lounger Pool Float, Translucent Inflatable Recliner Chair for Adults with Fast Inflation, Foot Rest & Cup Holder These products, both the dry float lounger and the socializer are prime examples of why I test products the way I do prior to writing my review.

When I initially received these products and inflated them I was fairly impressed with the design and comfort - by 18 days later both were flat lumps of rubber in the trash.

First the socializer never held air. After inflation by the following morning it had deflated to around 70% capacity. I put it under water in the pool and discovered multiple small defects in 2 seams.

The dry float lounger lasted a bit longer at 18 days but then was found flat due to a separation at the seam.

It is important to note neither of these were ever used by children or in any rough play as when I review products I adhere to strict guidelines - and there are no children in the home.

While the socializer is listed as a dry float it appears the user’s calves and feet would be in the water. The lounger pool float is perfect for those who prefer to float completely out of the water. When floating on this no part of the body is submerged in the water.

While 88-90% of the world’s population is right handed this manufacturer chose to place the cup holder on the left side and made it too small to hold a standard 12 Oz can for both of these floats. This is simply poor designing.

While these floats come with a small patch kit, these are only helpful when repairing a puncture and absolutely will not hold a torn seam.

While these floats appeared to have promise initially, in well under a month they proved to be poorly designed, and of substandard construction and materials.

I would not recommend either of these products.
text_fidelity_b: Swimways Dry Float Lounger Pool Float, Translucent Inflatable Recliner Chair for Adults with Fast Inflation, Foot Rest & Cup Holder

text_fidelity_a:
4M Snail Robot from KidzRobotics, A Fascinating Way to Learn About Mechanical Science! Build Your Very Own Pet Snail and Watch it Glide, Ages 8 I only paid $10 for this so I wasn't expecting lots, however I was expecting it to be decently made and a little more as described.

Putting that aside, if you plan to buy this I suggest you carefully look over the box and "in use" photos. On the box it does say you have to put the robot together and that it's meant for children over 8, those are very key points that I see were missed as I read the reviews. I wish I'd have really looked at the pictures myself, because I was expecting solid lines, not a bunch of dots, and from the given discription I thought the patterns would be more than just repeated crappy circles, also something you kind of see if you look at the pictures. Although even if you notice the pictures show dots and not lines, my dots were very widely spaced.

The things I couldn't have known from the pictures is how crappy it really is. The clear dome is thinner than your average disposable water bottle, everything that can be is shoddy plastic, and there is zero quality control. The wires on the one I got were attached to the wrong sides, thankfully they left the naked wires too long or it wouldn't have been useable at all because they needed to be crossed behind the motor to work at all. Plus, while this is technically buildable by children, the nuts, bolts and screws are so small that they are tricky to handle even for adults. It isn't hard to build at all, barely having enough parts to really be called buildable, so it isn't all that fantastic at what it's supposed to be, something to encourage children to think, build and experiment. Honestly if they included alternate uses or ways you can experiment with this it would be closer to worth while. Although since they sell other robots I guess that would cut into their bottom line.

This IS meant to be an educational toy, so it should be more educational, or not need to be put together at all and just be a toy. So if what you want is either a toy your kids will want to keep playing with, or a decent educationally toy, buy something else. We're hoping to find ways to experiment with ours, or at least hope the cats will find it fun.
text_fidelity_b: 4M Snail Robot from KidzRobotics, A Fascinating Way to Learn About Mechanical Science! Build Your Very Own Pet Snail and Watch it Glide, Ages 8

Bobby Fischer® Learn to Play Chess Set Board Game, Easy to Understand - How to Play Chess Book, 34 Plastic Staunton Chess Pieces, Folding Illustrated Chess Board, Family Games for Kids and Adults When I was in middle school, a teacher I did not really know invited me in to learn chess. It changed my life. I wanted to pass the information on to my kids, but it was hard to get them to make connections. This set is great.

WHAT IS THIS SET LIKE?
This set comes with a four fold board, big sized pieces, general instructions, and two dice.

BOARD
The board has information right on it, so that you don't have to repeat it over and over for visual learners.

PIECES
The pieces in this box are plenty big enough, have a nice felt bottom and are all in the box. Nothing was missing. There were even the two extra queens in the box too.

IS IT EASY TO TEACH WITH?
I found that this is really easy to teach with and in my case, it has been a while since I could play chess with someone and not a computer, so I found this very exciting.

DICE
The dice is a great way to even out playing with a beginner which helps a lot because who wants to be beaten constantly?

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a great set for a beginner chess learner. The board is small, the pieces easy to use and the directions clear and well laid out. The dice make it fun for mis matched players (beginner vs more advanced).

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I like this set and am glad to have it. My family is finally going to learn chess without me having to continually explain everything. The visuals are great.

Never Have I Ever Parent's Edition Card Game Set | Fun Game Night Party Games for Adults | for 2+ Players | Ages 17 + i thought this would be a fun gag game. If you are in mix company (right leaning vs left leaning), I would not recommend. The basic premise of the game is that each player votes on whether they think the card is true or false, but their votes don't actually matter. The person whose turn it is reads the card out loud, makes the final decision, and follows the action on the card (whether they are right or wrong). There is an action on the card for you to perform, which usually includes drinking.

First of all, this isn't much of a game because only 1 card out of 30 is false. There is so much content from the last four years and his numerous tweets that there is enough outrageous actions for all of the cards in the game. I was hoping for some outrageous cards that were false. So, you can laugh (or cringe) about all of the things he has done, but it doesn't make it fun since there isn't much strategy. If you guess that Trump said or did the things on the card, you will be right 95% of the time.

Then, on the lower right hand corner of each card you can tell if a statement is true or false depending on whether Trump is smiling or talking. Hopefully you have good eyes because they look very similar. Also, I know it is a total gag gift, but it makes no sense that the person that actually playing is the same person that is reading the card and the answer is staring them in the face.

If you are looking for an excuse to drink while reading Trump's crazy tweets over the last 4 years, this game is for you, but I can't imagine playing this game more than once.

text_fidelity_a:
Alex DIY Happy Little Loom Kit Kids Art and Craft Activity It's not wide enough to make a scarf, not for most kids. There is very little yarn included. You will need worsted weight for this kit.

The last point leads into my main issue with this. It does not provide enough information. You know you need yarn, but yarn varies in weight from lace (even gossamer) to super bulky. These terms refer to how thick the yarn is. Buy too thin, and the project will look terrible. Buy too thick and the yarn won't fit into the weft holes. You need worsted weight, and the only reason I know this is I knit and I recognized the yarn. The kit doesn't tell you.

If you hit a knot in the yarn, as I did, you should not keep going. Cut at the end of the row (the instructions don't tell you this) then start on the right side again (the instructions don't tell you this) and whenever you stop or start, leave a tail long enough to weave in later (nothing about weaving in tails is covered -- you're just supposed to know how to do that).

If you want to do the purse, for example, cut 15 strands at 32 inches each (not explained) so that they turn into 16 inch strands when doubled. You can get away with cutting 16 inch and having them single stranded, but it isn't optimal, especially when you are tying pairs at the end. And maybe do it with a yarn not in this kit. They barely provide enough yarn in this kit, and no one wants their kid playing yarn chicken and getting upset. It's cheap yarn. Get a good amount.

When you start the yarn, it is shipped in a center pull ball. While the value of balls is explained a little (I suppose over leaving it in a loose skein or hank to tangle on itself) the concept of center pull isn't touched on. Dig into the ball and get the end inside. That way the ball stays still while you work.

You don't really need the tool to guide the yarn back and forth, but it should have come with a comb to push it down and keep it even, a trick especially hard when you move the piece along down the thread. That's perhaps the biggest design flaw in this. It tends to make the work uneven because it's slid and it leaves gaps where the next section starts. That can mostly be worked out by blocking the piece after (another technique not covered -- wet it, stretch it into the shape you want and even out the rows, and pin it down to dry.)

This is a great kit for someone who already knows a lot about yarn projects like crochet or knitting, or of course weaving. For a first yarn craft, a kid is going to need some help, ideally from someone who knows a lot about yarn projects.
text_fidelity_b: Alex DIY Happy Little Loom Kit Kids Art and Craft Activity
